data.name: Dharanee
data.long_meaning: Dharani refers to the earth or ground. The name Dharanee means 'she who holds the earth'. It is derived from the Sanskrit word 'Dharana' which means 'to hold'. This name is used to honor the earth and represents stability and grounding energy.

data.cultural_impact: The name Dharanee holds a deep cultural significance in Hinduism as it connects to the reverence for the earth as a goddess and symbol of stability and fertility. This name honors the Earth Mother, remembering that we are all connected to the Earth and depend on it for our existence. In various Hindu rituals, the act of touching the earth or offering obeisance to the Earth Mother is believed to bring blessings and grounding energy.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Dharanee holds significant spiritual significance as it relates to the innate connection between the individual and the Earth Mother. In Hinduism, the Earth Goddess represents the material world, creation, and stability. The name Dharanee symbolizes the connection to this divine feminine presence that holds and sustains us. It serves as a reminder of our spiritual roots and our dependence on the Earth for our physical and spiritual existence.

historical_references.reference: The great Hindu epic, Mahabharata, describes Dharani as the goddess of the earth, who holds the seven mountains and their waters. She is invoked by the Pandava brothers during their final battle against the Kauravas.
In Puranic literature, Dharani is also known as Prithvi, the goddess of the earth. She is often depicted as the wife of Vishnu and the mother of Bhu-devi (goddess of the land).
